outcome: Adapt approved discovery, tutorials, difficulty and content presentation to player context — without covert manipulation or unfair advantage
overview: One-size player journeys overwhelm newcomers and underserve experienced players: tutorials are abandoned, good content goes undiscovered, and accessibility needs are missed. This solution adapts approved discovery, tutorials, challenge difficulty and content presentation to player context through a policy-and-fairness gate — no covert manipulation, no unfair advantage, no pay pressure — with player controls, age gates and explainability built in. Controlled tests over a 6–10-week pilot validate tutorial completion, content discovery and satisfaction gains while fairness and age-appropriate rules hold. Reference builds are specified for AWS and Azure, with Arabic-language content adaptation and Gulf data residency supported for regional titles.

benefits.text: Improve tutorial completion and early-session progression for new players in controlled tests
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Validated only in controlled experiments on the customer’s own onboarding flows — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Lift content discovery so more of the catalogue is actually played
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on the content taxonomy being complete enough to rank against player context

benefits.text: Serve accessibility and preference needs with player-controlled, explained adaptation
benefits.source: Reference design capability, Redington Gaming catalogue
benefits.limits: Adaptation quality depends on declared preferences and accessible content variants existing

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); player state and preferences remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No content taxonomy or approved content variants to adapt between
notFor.why: Personalisation can only rank and present what design has approved; without a taxonomy there is nothing safe to adapt

notFor.situation: Competitive modes where adaptation could alter fairness
notFor.why: Adapting difficulty or information in ranked play creates hidden advantage; the fairness gate blocks it, so there is no value to deliver there

notFor.situation: No experiment controls in the live game
notFor.why: Experience gains cannot be honestly attributed without controlled tests and a rollback path

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns adaptation policy, design ethics and age-gating approval · Duration: 6–10-week pilot; further 12–22 weeks to portfolio scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, personalisation engineer, game designer consultant; customer product owner, UX lead, accessibility reviewer, safety and privacy approvers · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and experience-baseline agreement
2) Context and taxonomy integration
3) Policy-gate and adaptation design
4) Controlled pilot on one journey
5) Fairness and accessibility review
6) Stabilisation and handover
